One resolver, no second precedence chain': `review_skill_lines` (plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-lookup.py, around line 170) calls `_areas.resolve_review_skill` once, prints `- <skill> (basis: <basis>, ...)` under `## Review skill`, and returns [] on a falsy skill. All other callers of `session_skills` and `writer_argv` are unchanged, because the new keyword defaults to False. I did not upgrade the word because (1) the helper itself refused to call it proved, and its stated reason is the missing fix run; (2) the basis carries a tally of 'SELFTEST FAILED: 979/980 cases passed', which cannot be four failing cases, so the red run's output is internally inconsistent as quoted; (3) the per-suite reds the executor's outcome quotes (audit-lookup 190/193, drive uy-block 63/64) have no command or stamp in `redFirst`. These are claims in prose, not recorded output, so I treat them as unverified. Quoted reason, verbatim: the fix run 'timed out after 54 s and its process group was torn down'. Nothing handed shows the cases passing or failing, so I did not mark it `not-proved`; the helper's recorded red is consistent with the cases being able to fail. The over-fire mutation results in the outcome (unconditional section fails rk4 and rk5; always adding fails vk3; never adding fails vk1) are monkeypatch runs in a scratch script and are not recorded anywhere I can read. I did not re-run them.
intent.inheritedTestsBasis: The bound is the single gate command `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_lookup.py tests/test_drive_phase.py`, a literal command that selects the whole of those two suite files. I did not read either suite in full; both are very large. I ran grep over both files for `reviewSkill` and `review.skill` and for `resolve_review_skill`. I opened `_skill_units` (tests/test_drive_phase.py:18025-18047) and `_step_rig`. Outside the task's own rk/vk cases, the only hit is tests/test_drive_phase.py:13219, the existing case about whether a phase review is due, which reads `reviewSkill`. It does not read the brief and does not read the session's argv. The existing sk1-sk3 cases pin only a task's own skills in the argv and would pass with the review-skill behaviour deleted, but they never claimed it. So no existing test in the gate set names the behaviour this task added. The two review-skill rk/vk blocks are the only coverage of it. This answer is from grep plus the reads named above, not from a full read of the suites. One shape worth knowing: vk1/vk2 monkeypatch `M.tree_head` and the `_step_rig` readers on a module copy loaded by name (`drive_phase_session_skills`), never restored. That is the file's existing pattern and I judged it isolated to that copy.
